content:
The [Dog Life Expectancy Calculator](/dog-life-expectancy-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. How long do dogs live? Life expectancy by breed size and age. Enter your breed size and current age (years) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

How long do dogs live? It depends mostly on size: small dogs typically live 12–16 years, medium dogs 10–13, large dogs 9–11 and giant dogs 7–9. Enter your dog's breed size and current age for its expected lifespan and the years it likely has left. The figures are published breed-size medians — an estimate, not a promise: weight, genetics, diet and veterinary care all move the real number. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Dog Life Expectancy Calculator

Start by choosing your breed size from the list, then entering your current age (years). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Pick your dog's breed size.
2. Enter its current age in years.
3. Read the expected lifespan, the typical range and the remaining years.

## How it works

The [Dog Life Expectancy Calculator](/dog-life-expectancy-calculator) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A 3-year-old medium dog has an expected lifespan of about 11.5 years (typical range 10–13), leaving about 8.5 years. Try the same figures in the [Dog Life Expectancy Calculator](/dog-life-expectancy-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Breed size: Medium (10–25 kg adult), Current age (years): 3), the [Dog Life Expectancy Calculator](/dog-life-expectancy-calculator) returns Expected lifespan: 11.5 years, Typical range: 10 – 13 years, Remaining years (estimate): 8.5 years. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. ## Why size matters so much

It is one of the clearest patterns in veterinary science: within dogs, larger breeds age faster and die younger than smaller ones — the opposite of the pattern across species. A 5 kg dog may live 15 years while a 50 kg dog of the same age is already old at 8. The gap is mostly about how fast large dogs grow and how much wear their bodies accumulate.

## What moves the number

Keeping a dog lean adds years — overweight dogs live measurably shorter lives. Breed matters inside a size band too (some breeds are prone to specific diseases), and regular vet care, dental care and exercise all help. The estimate here is a starting point, not a verdict.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Keeping your dog at a healthy weight is the biggest factor you control.
- The range matters more than the single number — most dogs land inside it.
- Ask your vet about your specific breed's common health issues.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long do dogs live on average?

About 10–13 years overall, but it depends on size: small dogs 12–16 years, medium 10–13, large 9–11 and giant breeds 7–9. Try it with your own numbers in the [Dog Life Expectancy Calculator](/dog-life-expectancy-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Do small dogs live longer than big dogs?

Yes — it is one of the clearest patterns in dogs. Small breeds routinely outlive giant breeds by five or more years. Try it with your own numbers in the [Dog Life Expectancy Calculator](/dog-life-expectancy-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How can I help my dog live longer?

Keep it lean, exercise it daily, keep up with vet check-ups and dental care, and know your breed's common health problems so they are caught early. Try it with your own numbers in the [Dog Life Expectancy Calculator](/dog-life-expectancy-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the Dog Life Expectancy Calculator?

Just Breed size and Current age (years). Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
